title: Contain a bad route before it becomes a global incident
description: Select a routing-policy candidate, inject a provider fault, and choose a recovery boundary. The lab projects retries, circuit state, fallback quality, cancellation waste, cost, and rollout verdict.

releases.label: Balanced routing v18
releases.detail: A tested route mix with small quality and cost improvements.

releases.label: Cheapest-route v19
releases.detail: Lower estimated cost, but offline task quality regresses materially.

releases.label: New adapter v20
releases.detail: Promising initial results from too few evaluated requests.

faults.label: Healthy provider
faults.detail: Normal transient errors and a small share of client disconnects.

faults.label: Provider throttling
faults.detail: A burst produces retryable throttles and raises attempt pressure.

faults.label: Mid-stream disconnects
faults.detail: Connections often close after partial output has already been generated.

faults.label: Regional outage
faults.detail: Most primary attempts fail until the route circuit ejects the region.

policies.label: Blind retries and shared cache
policies.detail: Retry every failure, keep the route open, ignore upstream cancellation, and cache by prompt alone.

policies.label: Bounded retry and route circuit
policies.detail: Retry classified transient failures once, propagate cancellation, deduplicate client intent, and eject only the failing route.

policies.label: Fail fast without fallback
policies.detail: Do not retry or fall back; open the route circuit early and return an explicit degraded response.
